jobs.description: Employer: Evergy Expires: 10/05/2026 SUMMARY OF JOB RESPONSIBILITIES AND REQUIREMENTS JOB TITLE: Intern – Transmission Line Engineering REQUISITION: TRA0106DEPARTMENT: Transmission Engineering – Topeka General OfficeLOCATION: Topeka, KSPAY RANGE: $23.00 - $28.00 / Hour Full-Time Internship Position for Summer 2027 Scheduled Work Hours: Monday - Friday, 8:00 a.m. - 5:00 p.m. (Other hours as required) It's never too early to start exploring your future career. If you're ready to apply the principles you've been learning in the classroom to real-world projects, Evergy is for you. Hands-on experience is what our internship programs are all about. Our programs provide students with meaningful experience while helping Evergy identify talented future full-time employees. Many of our interns transition to successful careers at Evergy.Evergy interns are trusted contributors on active design projects. In addition to project work, Evergy interns participate in many social and extra-curricular activities, including volunteer events, power plant tours, Lunch-and-Learns, and more. Intern Description:This position joins a skilled, energetic, and engaging team of engineers who perform all aspects of high-voltage (69kV-345kV) transmission line design; a fast-paced, dynamic, and highly specialized engineering discipline. Each “T-line” project is unique. The long, linear nature of these facilities requires engineers to solve a variety of challenges, making thoughtful engineering judgment as valuable as technical analysis. Interns are trusted contributors on active engineering projects. They gain exposure to coordinating and collaborating with professionals in other departments and work locations. Interns participate in technical conversations and meetings with project managers and other professionals on the project team. They visit Evergy transmission line projects in the field before, during, and after construction. Construction site visits provide the opportunity to see transmission linemen, some of the most highly skilled and valued workers in the construction industry, at their craft. Typical intern responsibilities include:Perform detailed line design and analysis using PLS-CADD and PLS-POLE, highly sophisticated finite element software packages used exclusively for transmission line engineering.Create structure loading drawings and review vendor-produced calculations and structure drawings.Design and analyze transmission line foundation systems, including deep drilled piers and embedded structures.Conduct construction site visits to perform safety observations and gain familiarity with the practical application of engineering deliverables.Incorporate and interpret transmission line survey data, including aerial LiDAR, ground survey information, and easement exhibits.Collaborate with the transmission line engineering team and other Evergy teams, including Permitting & Environmental, Substation Engineering, Real Estate, Project Management, and Construction & Maintenance.Prepare construction drawings, bill of material packages, and supporting construction documents.Analyze existing facility structural capacity and electrical clearance margins in accordance with code and company standards. Education and Experience Requirements:Candidates must be currently enrolled in a university with an ABET-accredited engineering program in one of the following or a related technical field: Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or Electrical Engineering. Skills, Knowledge, and Abilities Required:A demonstrated ability to overcome challenges and contribute effectively as part of a collaborative project team.An inquisitive, analytical mindset, with a desire to understand the reasoning behind design standards and the perspectives of diverse stakeholders.Strong organizational, written, and verbal communication skills.Understanding of fundamental engineering principles and advanced mathematics.Proficiency with spreadsheets, word processing, and database software.Ability to evaluate, select, and apply standard engineering techniques, procedures, and criteria while exercising sound engineering judgment. Working Conditions:Primarily an office setting with standard business hours (Monday-Friday). Periodic visits to transmission line and substation field environments are also expected. jobs.description: Employer: Naval Research Laboratory Expires: 10/09/2026 *Note: Position seeks Graduate Student (either MS or PhD)*About NRL: The U.S. Naval Research Laboratory (NRL) serves as the corporate research laboratory for the Navy, Marine Corps, and the broader Department of War. Operating since 1923, the laboratory conducts basic and applied research to deliver groundbreaking science and technology that ensures a decisive, asymmetric edge for the warfighter. Its innovative work spans domains from the depths of the ocean to the vastness of space, historically producing pioneering advancements such as the development of radar and onion routingAbout the Team: The Electronic Warfare Support Measures (ESM) Branch is engaged in the research and development (R&D) of advanced passive electronic warfare systems. Code 5720 employees conduct R&D, prototype design, and operational testing of ESM systems/subsystems associated with all disciplines of modern ESM systems. The ESM Branch at NRL has a long history of directly supporting the warfighter through a combination of long term system developments as well as the delivery of quick reaction capabilities (QRC). The ESM Branch also provides support to the Intelligence Community, particularly in the area of special signal collection. Research Activity Areas: • Digital Receiver Design and Implementation • Advanced Digital Signal Processing • Precision Direction Finding (PDF) Techniques • Precision Passive Geolocation Techniques • Miniaturized ES Payloads for Unmanned Platforms • RF Design (Board and System Level)About the Job: The incumbent will work conduct budget and financial work utilizing Microsoft Office. They will also perform various functions such as preparing forms, logging documents, reviewing travel orders, and organizing data. They will prepare a wide range of documents in final format. About you: This position is responsible for creating state of the art software for electronic support (ES), typically embedded in experimental real-time hardware systems. The position requires software engineering skills including reading, writing, editing, testing, troubleshooting, and validating C++ software. The position also requires designing, implementing and validating new capabilities, teamwork, and effective oral and written communication. In addition to proficiency in C++, candidates should have experience in one or more of the following: Matlab, Python, Java, Cuda, Qt/Qc. Job SummaryTunnel 9 is a geographically separated unit of Arnold Engineering Development Complex (AEDC). It provides aerodynamic simulation capabilities critical to hypersonic-system and vehicle-technology development at speeds from Mach 7 to Mach 18.The BNH Internship Program offers full-time summer internship opportunities lasting 10 to 12 weeks for undergraduate and graduate engineering students. Interns are paired with experienced engineers and scientists who mentor them while they complete assigned projects, gain practical experience in their field of study, and contribute to the Air Force and BNH missions. Interns will brief senior management summarizing work accomplished, lessons learned and recommended next actions. Job Duties:The Tunnel 9 internship provides interns with multiple projects throughout the summer, exposing them to the range of engineering work performed at AEDC Tunnel 9. Assignments address practical engineering challenges that support Air Force and BNH missions. Examples of previous and planned intern assignments include the following; this list is illustrative and not exhaustive:Operate and conduct tests in Tunnel 9’s research and development (R&D) Mach 3 tunnel and install test article hardware and instrumentation in support of active customer testing at Mach 7–18.Validate test article data-acquisition system configurations and nomenclature; conduct pre-test instrumentation integrity checks; and perform model hardware changes between test runs.Support the development and application of temperature-sensitive paint, infrared thermography, fast-response piezoelectric force-balance instrumentation, balance-calibration software, and test article boundary-layer transition measurements and analysis.Develop graphical user interfaces to process, analyze, and decode test article and tunnel-facility data; develop or modify hardware and software interfaces for integrated data-acquisition and processing systems; and repair malfunctioning test article instrumentation.Create and modify electrical schematics using AutoCAD; research power load-bank systems for potential use with emergency generator systems; and assist with the field implementation, validation, and verification of new or modified measurement, data-acquisition, and control systems.Improve or add limit indicators to network and facility human-machine interface (HMI) screens; analyze optical measurement systems and recommend upgrades from analog drive motors to stepper-motor technology; and develop or modify programmable logic controller (PLC) ladder logic and HMI screens for facility control systems.Configure and program digital servo amplifiers and other facility control-system hardware; develop improved system-controller interfaces; and perform system integration, checkout, troubleshooting, drawing redlines, and work-instruction improvements for test cell systems.Research and prepare technical documentation and recommendations for operationally feasible dew-point measurement hardware; develop portable electronic devices for timing and calibrating high-speed camera systems; and build servo-valve models in MATLAB Simulink.Create three-dimensional models of subsystem components in PTC Creo; design and 3D-print fixtures for alignment, installation, and gauge inspections; design large hardware carts for assembly work; and improve and document 3D-printing methods to increase print accuracy.Refine heat-transfer code for improved integration with ANSYS and Creo; conduct material, structural, and thermo-structural analyses using ANSYS; and design hardware to support test cell and test article customer-testing activities.Update statistical probability-of-failure analyses for high-pressure vessels rated from 20,000 to 60,000 psi; and perform field verification of hydraulic-unit drawings and engineering checks of control schematics. Minimum Requirements for Consideration:IMPORTANT: Resumes must include degree program, projected graduation date, and GPA to be considered. We will not be reaching out to obtain information that was requested but not included. Basic Qualifications:Must be currently enrolled in an accredited university and pursuing a degree in one of the following disciplines:At least sophomore status (45 credit hours) completed by May 2027Minimum GPA of 2.75Ability to work 40 hours each week for 12 weeks from May to August. This is a full-time temporary position, so no vacation is accrued. We encourage students to take personal vacations before reporting and between the term ending and their return to school.Must have the ability to travel between multiple facilities and buildings within the industrial complex to support test operations.Must be able to obtain and maintain a security clearance and the AEDC local area networkDue to Air Force Security requirements, U.S. Citizenship is required for employment at AEDCMechanical EngineeringElectrical EngineeringMechatronics EngineeringComputer EngineeringComputer Science or Software Engineering (hard programmers, business systems, data science, Power Platform developers, or machine learning interests; cybersecurity students need to have Security+)Industrial EngineeringAerospace Engineering Preferred QualificationsDemonstrate a positive, self-driven, and adaptable approach; show intellectual curiosity; accept feedback; work effectively with minimal direction.Communicate effectively and demonstrate a willingness to expand technical knowledge and learn new skills.Possess experience with, or familiarity with, PTC Creo, AutoCAD, ANSYS, Excel, MATLAB, and/or 3D-printing equipment and processes.Be able to read, create, and modify mechanical drawings and electrical schematics, including wire tables and cable instrumentation documentation.Show an interest in supporting the nation’s defense; an active security clearance is preferred. Join our Team! U.S. Citizenship is required. At this time BNH will not sponsor any applicants for employment authorization or offer any immigration related support for this position (i.e. H1b, F1 OPT, F-1 STEM OPT, F-1 CPT, J-1, E-2, E-3, L-1, or other forms of work authorization that require immigration support from an employer). The minimum and maximum full-time annual salaries for this role are listed below, by location. Please note that this salary information is solely for candidates hired to perform work within one of these locations and refers to the amount BNH is willing to pay at the time of this posting. Salaries for part-time jobs will be adjusted based upon the number of hours agreed to work. M06: $36.29 - $49.90/ per hour at location Maryland: AEDC White Oak Campus MD BNH is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibit discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, veteran status, and any other grounds for discrimination prohibited by applicable law. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training

jobs.description: Employer: Pella Corporation Expires: 10/09/2026 Plant Process Engineering Intern - Summer 2027Program Duration: End of May - Early AugustLocation: Multiple Locations (on-site) including Pella, IA, Macomb, IL & Sioux Center, IA Pella Corporation is seeking motivated engineering students for our Plant Process Engineering Internship at one our manufacturing facilities.This internship provides hands-on experience working on real manufacturing challenges and improvement opportunities. Interns collaborate with engineers, operations leaders, and production teams to improve processes, reduce waste, increase efficiency, and support manufacturing initiatives.If you're interested in applying engineering principles in a manufacturing environment, leading meaningful projects, and gaining experience similar to that of an entry-level engineer, we'd love to connect with you.ResponsibilitiesResponsibilitiesAs a Plant Process Engineering Intern, you will support manufacturing operations through project work focused on process improvement, problem solving, quality enhancement, and operational efficiency. Interns are given ownership of meaningful projects and work alongside experienced engineers and mentors to develop technical, professional, and leadership skills.Responsibilities are similar to what we expect of entry-level engineers who join Pella after graduation.As a Plant Process Engineering Intern, you may:Modify and improve manufacturing processes to improve quality, increase reliability, reduce costs, and eliminate wasteSupport continuous improvement initiatives using problem-solving and engineering methodologiesDevelop or enhance manufacturing processes, equipment, and toolingSpecify, design, and procure equipment required to support manufacturing and new product initiativesImplement new processes from concept through productionAnalyze manufacturing data and recommend solutions that improve operational performancePartner with engineering, operations, maintenance, quality, and other cross-functional teams to support business objectives Preferred Degree AreasMechanical EngineeringIndustrial EngineeringManufacturing EngineeringAgricultural EngineeringIndustrial TechnologyOther related engineering disciplinesQualificationsQualificationsCurrently pursuing a bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline. Preferred majors are listed above.Strong academic standingDemonstrated leadership, teamwork, or involvement through campus organizations, work experience, athletics, volunteer activities, or other experiencesProficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and OutlookExperience with CAD software such as Solid Edge, AutoCAD, or similar platforms preferredStrong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to effectively communicate with both technical and non-technical audiencesDemonstrated problem-solving and analytical skillsExperience leading projects, initiatives, or team efforts from planning through execution preferredAbility to succeed in a fast-paced, collaborative environment Compensation: The starting pay rate for this position is $27.90 per hour. Compensation for this role is established through Pella Corporation’s internship program. Eligible participants may receive transition assistance in accordance with company policies and program guidelines.
